p0.original: 关键问题：如何测量智力
p0.en: Key issue: How to measure intelligence

p2.original: 智力测验在历史上备受争议，现在大多数心理学家都将智力看作一种呈正态分布的特质，并且可以通过各种认知任务的绩效来测量。
p2.en: The intellectual test has been controversial in history, and most psychologists now see intelligence as a normal distribution feature and can be measured by the performance of various cognitive tasks.

p3.original: 心理学家一直都执着于研究人们在推理、问题解决和创新思维等能力上的个体差异。然而，对个体差异的评估并不是从现代心理学才开始的。历史记载显示，中国古代就曾使用过成熟的心理测验方法。中国古人使用一种文官考核程序，要求政府官员每三年参加一场口试来证明自己的能力。后来，申请人要参加文官考核笔试，以评估其在法律、军事、农业和地理方面的知识。19世纪初被派往中国的英国外交官和传教士均赞叹这个选拔程序，以至于英国人和后来的美国人在选拔公务员时都采用了这个中国选拔系统的改编版本（Wiggins，1973）。
p3.en: Psychologists have been dedicated to studying individual differences in people's abilities in terms of reasoning, problem resolution and innovative thinking. However, the assessment of individual differences does not begin with modern psychology. Historical records show that China has used mature methods of psychological testing in ancient times. The ancient Chinese use a civilian examination procedure, which requires government officials to take an oral test every three years to prove their competence. Applicants are subsequently required to take a civil examination to assess their legal, military, agricultural and geographical knowledge. Both British diplomats and missionaries sent to China at the beginning of the nineteenth century admired the selection process so that the English and later Americans used the modified version of the Chinese selection system in their selection of civil servants (Wiggins, 1973).

p4.original: 然而，与历史上的中国人不同，现代美国人更感兴趣的似乎是人们的“聪明”程度，而不是他们学到了多少东西。正是这种对“先天能力”的兴趣推动了我们今天所知的智力测验的发展。不过，尽管智力测验有着悠久历史，而且在当今社会已被广泛使用，智力（intelligence）这个术语的确切含义仍存在争议（Neisser et al.，1996）。尽管如此，大多数心理学家可能会同意这个笼统的定义——智力是获取知识、推理和有效解决问题的心理能力。他们也会同意，必须通过对个体完成各种不同任务进行测量来全面了解其智力。但是，对于到底哪些心理能力构成了智力，以及这些能力的数量与占比多少，他们还存在分歧。
p4.en: However, unlike the Chinese in history, modern Americans seem to be more interested in people's “smartness” than in how much they learn. It is this interest in “ingenuity” that has driven the development of the intellectual tests we know today. However, despite the long history of intellectual testing and the widespread use of the term intelligence in today's society, the exact meaning of the term is still controversial (Neisser et al., 1996). Nevertheless, most psychologists may agree with this general definition of intelligence as the mental ability to acquire knowledge, reason and effectively solve problems. They would also agree that a full understanding of the individual's intelligence is required by measuring the different tasks performed by the individual. However, they still differ as to which mental abilities constitute intellectual capacity and the number and proportion of those abilities.

p5.original: 每个人都认同，智力是相对而言的。也就是说，一个人的智力水平必须是相对于一个（通常是相同年龄段的）参照群体在相同维度上的能力而言的。每个人也都会同意，智力是一种假设构念（hypothetical construct）：一种不能直接观察而必须从行为中进行推断的特征。在实践中，这意味着智力是根据个体在智力测验中的反应来测量的。之后，把个体分数与参照群体的分数进行比较。这些测验究竟应该测量什么是许多争议的根源。思考这个核心概念：
p5.en: Everyone agrees that intelligence is relative. This means that a person's intellectual level must be in relation to the ability of a reference group (usually of the same age group) to have the same dimensions. Everyone would agree that intelligence is a hypothetical construct: a characteristic that cannot be directly observed but must be inferred from behaviour. In practice, this means that intelligence is measured on the basis of an individual's reaction to an intellectual test. The individual scores are then compared with those of the reference group. These tests should measure what is at the root of many of the controversy. Think about this core concept:

p6.original: 智力测验在历史上备受争议，现在大多数心理学家都将智力看作一种呈正态分布的特质，并且可以通过各种认知任务的绩效来测量。
p6.en: The intellectual test has been controversial in history, and most psychologists now see intelligence as a normal distribution feature and can be measured by the performance of various cognitive tasks.

p7.original: 我们将先向你介绍智力测验的创始人，以此来开始对智力和智力测验的探讨。
p7.en: We will start by introducing you to the founders of the intellectual tests, so that we can begin the discussion of the intellectual and intellectual tests.

p9.original: 6.8 找出比奈-西蒙测验的4个重要特点。
p9.en: 6.8 Identification of four important features of the Binai-Simon test.

p10.original: 6.9 讨论智商的现代概念和测量的发展。
p10.en: 6.9 Discuss the development of modern concepts and measurements of IQ.

p11.original: 6.8 比奈和西蒙发明了学校能力测验
p11.en: 6.8 Bennet and Simon invented the school competency test.

p13.original: 找出比奈-西蒙测验的4个重要特点。
p13.en: We've got four important features of the Bene-Simon test.

p14.original: 阿尔弗雷德·比奈（Alfred Binet）及其同事西奥多·西蒙（Théodore Simon）于1904年进入大众的视野。当时，一项新法律要求所有法国儿童都要上学，而政府希望有一种方法可以识别那些需要特殊补习帮助的儿童。比奈和西蒙应邀为此设计一个测验。他们设计了30个问题，测试了上学所需的各种能力（见表6-2）。这个新方法是成功的：它确实预测了哪些儿童能应对正常的学校学习，而哪些儿童不能。
p14.en: Alfred Binet and his colleague Théodore Simon entered the public view in 1904. At that time, a new law required all French children to attend school, and the Government hoped that there would be a way to identify those children who needed special remedial assistance. Bennet and Simon were invited to design a test for this. They designed 30 questions and tested the competencies required for school attendance (see table 6-2). This new approach has been successful: it does predict which children can cope with normal schooling and which cannot.

p15.original: 表6-2 首版比奈-西蒙测验的题目举例
p15.en: Table 6-2 Examples of topics for the first Bene-Simon test

p16.original: 比奈-西蒙测验具有4个重要特点（Binet，1911）。
p16.en: The Bene-Simon test has four important features (Binet, 1911).

p17.original: 1. 他们将测验分数解释为对当前表现的估计，而不是对先天智力的测量。
p17.en: 1. They interpret test scores as estimates of current performance rather than measurements of congenital intelligence.

p18.original: 2. 他们希望使用测验分数来找出需要特殊帮助的儿童，而不仅仅是将儿童归类或标记为聪明或迟钝。
p18.en: 2. They wish to use test scores to identify children in need of special help, not just to classify or label children as smart or retarded.

p19.original: 3. 他们强调，训练和机遇都可能会影响智力，而且他们想要通过这个测验找出特殊教育可以在哪些领域帮助某些儿童提高成绩。
p19.en: 3. They stressed that both training and opportunities can affect mentality and that they want to see through this test where special education can help some children to improve their performance.

p20.original: 4. 他们凭经验建构测验——根据观察到的儿童表现——而不是将测验与某个特定的智力理论挂钩。
p20.en: They use empirical construction tests — based on observed child performance — rather than linking them to a particular intellectual theory.

p21.original: 比奈和西蒙用这个测验测量了不同年龄的法国儿童，并首次计算了每个年龄的平均分数。之后，他们将每个儿童的表现与不同年龄段儿童的平均表现进行了比较，得出一个分数，并用心理年龄（mental age，MA）这个术语来表示。举例来说，当一个儿童的分数与一组5岁儿童的平均分数相同时，不管他或她的生理年龄（chronological age，CA）是多少，我们都会说这个儿童的心理年龄是5岁。比奈和西蒙揭示了最需要补习帮助的是那些心理年龄落后于生理年龄两岁的学生。
p21.en: Bene and Simon used the test to measure French children of different ages and for the first time calculated the average score per age. They then compare the performance of each child with the average performance of children of different age groups, arrive at a score and use the term mental age (mental age, MA). For example, when a child has the same score as the average for a group of five-year-olds, regardless of his or her biological age (chronogenic age, CA), we would say that the child's mental age is five. Binai and Simon revealed that the most in need of remedial assistance were students of two years of age who were behind their biological age.

p22.original: 6.9 美国心理学家借用比奈和西蒙的观点
p22.en: 6.9 The American psychologist borrowed the views of Bennet and Simon.

p24.original: 讨论智商的现代概念和测量的发展。
p24.en: To discuss the development of modern concepts and measurements of IQ.

p25.original: 在法国人开始对学校儿童施测后不到十年，美国心理学家引进了比奈-西蒙的学校能力测验，并将其改进为我们现在所说的智商测验（IQ test）。为此，他们修订了计分程序，增加了测验内容，获得了一个庞大的标准组（包括成年人）的分数来为分数创建比较了水平。美国人普遍接受过智力测验，他们把它当作一种技术，并用“智力测验”分数来描述自己和他人。
p25.en: Less than 10 years after the French began testing school children, American psychologists introduced the Bene-Simon school competency test and improved it to what we now call an IQ test (IQ test). To that end, they revised the score-counting procedures, increased the test content and obtained a large standard group (including adults) to create a comparable level of scores. Americans have generally been tested for intelligence, which they see as a technique and describe themselves and others with “intellectual test” scores.

p26.original: 6.9.1 智力测验在美国的吸引力
p26.en: 6.9.1 Attractiveness of intellectual tests in the United States

p27.original: 为什么智力测验在美国如此流行？20世纪初，有三股力量改变了美国的面貌，它们合到一起，使得智力测验看起来像一种摆脱动荡和不确定性的有序方式。
p27.en: Why is the intelligence test so popular in America? At the beginning of the twentieth century, three forces changed the face of the United States, and together they brought together to make intelligence tests look like an orderly way out of turmoil and uncertainty.

p28.original: 1. 美国正经历着一场由全球性经济、社会和政治危机所引发的前所未有的移民潮。
p28.en: 1. The United States is experiencing an unprecedented wave of migration triggered by the global economic, social and political crisis.

p29.original: 2. 新法律要求普及教育——所有儿童都要上学，使得学生大量涌入学校。
p29.en: The new law called for universal education — all children were going to school — resulting in a massive influx of students into schools.

p30.original: 3. 第一次世界大战开始时，军方需要一种对新兵进行评估和分类的方法。
p30.en: 3. At the beginning of the First World War, the military needed a method of assessing and classifying new recruits.

p31.original: 这些事件加起来促使对大量人群进行评估的需求大增（Chapman，1988）。智力不仅被看作一种为社会剧变的动荡带来秩序的手段；而且还被看作一种低廉、民主的方式，来区分谁能或谁不能从教育或军事领导力培训中获益。
p31.en: Together, these events have led to a significant increase in the need to assess large numbers of people (Chapman, 1988). Intellectuals are not only seen as a means of bringing order to social upheavals; It is also seen as a cheap, democratic way of distinguishing between those who can or cannot benefit from education or military leadership training.

p32.original: 美国的大规模团体测验计划造成了两个后果。一个是公众开始认同智力测验能准确地根据心理能力来对人们进行区分。这很快导致学校和工厂广泛使用测验。另一个更不幸的后果是，测验强化了主流偏见。具体来说，军队报告表明，测验分数的差异与种族和原国籍有关（Yerkes，1921）。当然，这样的统计数据也可以被用于证明劣势环境限制了人们智力能力的全面发展。然而，这个测验导致的结果却是那些很少接触英语（测试使用的唯一语言）或对如何参加此类测验知之甚少的移民被贴上了“白痴”“笨蛋”和“低能儿”（当时用来说明不同程度智力障碍的术语）的标签。
p32.en: The large-scale group testing programme in the United States had two consequences. One is that the public begins to identify with the ability of people to accurately distinguish according to their mental abilities. This quickly led to widespread use of testing in schools and factories. Another more unfortunate consequence is that the tests reinforce the prevailing bias. Specifically, military reports indicate that differences in test scores are related to race and origin (Yerkes, 1921). Such statistics can, of course, also be used to prove that disadvantaged environments limit the full development of people's intellectual capacities. However, the result of this test is that immigrants who have little contact with English (the only language used in the tests) or who have little knowledge of how to participate in such tests are labelled as “wits” “wits” and “incompetents” (the term used at the time to describe different degrees of intellectual impairment).

p33.original: 虽然对现在的我们来说，这些问题显而易见（有后见偏差的帮助），但在当时，这些问题被掩盖了，因为智力测验满足了当时大多数人的需求：它们施测方便，并提供了一种根据分数来对人们进行评估和分类的方式。因此，公众普遍认为这些测验是客观和公正的。
p33.en: Although these problems are obvious to us now (with the help of backward bias), they were masked at that time, because the intellectual tests met the needs of the majority at that time: they were easy to measure and provided a way of assessing and classifying people on the basis of scores. Thus, the public generally considered the tests to be objective and impartial.

p35.original: 美国最受推崇的新智力测验，出自斯坦福大学路易斯·推孟（Lewis Terman）教授实验室。为了美国在校儿童，他对比奈-西蒙测验进行了改编，标准化了施测程序和年龄段规范。结果便形成了斯坦福-比奈智力量表（Stanford-Binet Intelligence Scale，Terman，1916）。这个测验很快成了评判其他智力测量的标准。但由于必须单独施测，推孟的测验不如团体测验那般经济划算。尽管如此，它更能发现学习问题。更重要的是，斯坦福-比奈智力测验设计有儿童版和成人版。
p35.en: The most popular new intelligence test in the United States is from the Professor Lewis Terman Laboratory of Stanford University. For school children in the United States, he had adapted the Pinai-Simon test to standardize the application process and age-group norms. As a result, the Stanford-Binet Inteligence System (Stanford-Binet Information Scale, Terman, 1916) was formed. The test quickly became the criterion for other intellectual measurements. However, because of the need for separate testing, the test is less economical than the group test. Nevertheless, it is more likely to identify learning problems. More importantly, the Stanford-Binai intelligence test was designed to have a child and adult version.

p36.original: 在新测验中，推孟引入了智力商数（intelligence quotient，IQ，简称智商）。这个概念最初由德国心理学家威廉姆·斯特恩（William Stern）于1914年提出。智商等于心理年龄与生理年龄的比值乘以100（以消除小数）：
p36.en: In the new test, the Intelligence quatient, IQ, IQ, was introduced in Thin Meng. The concept was first introduced by the German psychologist William Stern in 1914. The IQ is equal to the ratio of mental to biological age multiplied by 100 (to eliminate decimals):

p37.original: 请通过以下例子来了解智商公式：假定一个儿童的生理年龄是8岁，其测验分数表明其心理年龄是10岁。将心理年龄除以生理年龄（MA/CA = 10/8）得到1.25，再乘以100，得到智商为125。相比之下，另一个生理年龄为8岁的儿童，在测验中表现出6岁的平均水平，根据推孟的公式，其智商为6/8×100 = 75。那些心理年龄与生理年龄相同的人，智商分数为100，这被认为是平均或“正常”智商。
p37.en: Please learn about the IQ formula by using the following example: assuming that a child is 8 years old, the test scores indicate that his/her mental age is 10 years. Divide the mental age by the biological age (MA/CA = 10/8) and multiply it by 100 and obtain IQ 125. In contrast, another child of 8 years of biological age showed an average of 6 years of age in the test, with an IQ of 6/8 x 100 = 75, according to the quince formula. Those of the same mental age and biological age have an IQ of 100, which is considered to be average or “normal”.

p38.original: 不久后，这个新的斯坦福-比奈测验便成了临床心理学、精神病学和教育咨询领域的流行工具。随着测验的发表，推孟还宣传了自己的理念，即智力在很大程度上是与生俱来的，是可以测量的。这里面传达的信息是，智商分数反映了人的一些基本的、不变的东西。
p38.en: Shortly thereafter, the new Stanford-Bina test became a popular tool in the fields of clinical psychology, psychiatry and educational counselling. As the tests were published, Thémon also promoted his idea that intelligence was largely inherent and measurable. The message is that IQ scores reflect some basic, constant things about people.

p39.original: 尽管斯坦福-比奈测验成了智力测验的“黄金标准”，但它也受到了批评。最大的反对意见是，它采用了不一致的智力定义，因为它在不同年龄段测量的是不同的心理能力。例如，它对2～4岁儿童测量的是操纵物体的能力，而对成年人测量的几乎都是语言项目。测验编制人员注意到了这些批评，而且随着对智力的科学理解的增强，心理学家认识到，在所有年龄段都测量多种智力能力这一点越来越重要。斯坦福-比奈测验的一个现代修订版，现在能给出各种心理能力各自的分数。
p39.en: Although the Stanford-Bina test became the “gold standard” for intelligence tests, it was also criticized. The biggest objection was that it used an inconsistent definition of intelligence, since it measured different mental abilities at different ages. For example, it measures the ability to manipulate objects for children aged 2 to 4 years, while almost all measurements of adults are language projects. Test preparers have taken note of these criticisms and, as scientific understanding of intelligence has increased, psychologists have recognized the growing importance of measuring multiple mental abilities at all ages. A modern revised version of the Stanford-Bina test now gives scores for each of the mental abilities.

p41.original: 心理学家开始将智商公式用于成年人后，智商公式的一个内在问题便立马凸显出来。情况是这样的：到了青少年中晚期，随着人们的心理在许多不同方面都得到了发展，心理年龄分数通常会趋于稳定。因此，测验所测量的心理成长，似乎有所放缓（例如，15岁时的心理年龄和30岁时的心理年龄可能差不多）计算智商的推孟公式会导致一个奇怪的结果，正常儿童长大后会成为一个有智力缺陷的成年人——至少就他们的测验分数而言！如果测验测得到一个30岁人的心理年龄停留在他15岁时的水平，请注意他的智商分数会是这样：
p41.en: Once psychologists begin to apply IQ formulas to adults, an inherent problem with IQ formulas becomes apparent. This is the case: in the middle and late stages of adolescence, the mental age score tends to stabilize as people's minds develop in many different ways. Thus, the psychological growth measured by the tests seems to have slowed (e.g., the mental age at age 15 and the mental age at age 30 may be similar) to calculate the IQ push formula, leading to a strange result that normal children grow up to become adults with intellectual impairments — at least in terms of their test scores! If the test shows that a 30-year-old person's mental age remains at his 15-year-old age, please note that his IQ score would be as follows:

p42.original: 心理学家很快就意识到，这种对成年人心理能力的描绘是错误的。人们成人后，头脑并不会逐渐笨拙（尽管他们的孩子有时会这样认为）。谨慎起见，心理学家决定放弃原来的智商公式，并且开始寻求另一种计算智商的方法。他们的解决方案类似于常见的“按曲线计分”的做法。我们需要对这条著名的曲线做一些解释。
p42.en: Psychologists quickly realized that this picture of the mental capacity of adults was wrong. People do not grow clumsy when they are adults (although their children sometimes think so). The psychologist decided to abandon the original IQ formula and to begin looking for another method of calculating IQ. Their solutions are similar to the common “curve-by-curve” approach. We need some explanation of this famous curve.

p44.original: 计算智商的新方法背后的假定是，智力是呈正态分布的。换句话说，假定人群的智力呈现出不同程度的分布，因此只有少数人位于高分段或低分段，大多数人聚集在中心平均值附近。在这一点上，智力就像许多身体特质（包括身高、体重和鞋码）一样（见图6-6）。如果你要针对其中某一维度对一大群人施测，那么你可能就会得到一组遵循“曲线”的分数，该曲线与老师用于“按曲线”评分的曲线相同。
p44.en: The assumption behind the new method of calculating IQ is that intelligence is distributed correctly. In other words, assuming a different degree of distribution of people's mentalities, only a small number of people are located in high or low segments, and the majority are concentrated near the central average. At this point, intelligence is like many physical qualities (including height, weight and shoe codes) (see figures 6-6). If you want to measure a large group of people for a given dimension, you may get a set of points that follow the curve, which is the same as the curve that teachers use to rate by the curve.

p45.original: 图6-6 理解正态分布的概念
p45.en: Figure 6-6 Understanding the concept of normal distribution

p46.original: 更确切地说，在对大量个体进行智力测验时，每个年龄段的分数都呈正态分布。（所有年龄的成年人都被分到一组，他们的分数分布也符合这种钟形曲线。）可以画表格来显示测验分数落在这个正态曲线上的什么位置，现在可以用这个表格的数据来确定智商，而不使用旧智商公式来计算智商。这些分数经过了统计校正，因此每个年龄组的平均数都设在100。接近于分布中央的分数（通常位于90～110）属于正常范围（normal range，见图6-6）；位于分布一端低于70的分数属于智力障碍（intellectual disability）的范围；而位于分布另一端高于130的分数有时表明被试是天才（giftedness）。请花些时间研究一下图6-6，以便更好地理解这一概念。
p46.en: More precisely, the scores for each age group are fairly distributed when a large number of individuals are tested. (All adults of all ages are divided into groups and their fraction distribution corresponds to this bell curve. ) A table can be drawn to show where the test scores fall on this normal curve, and the data in this table can now be used to determine IQ rather than using the old IQ formula to calculate IQ. These scores have been statistically corrected, so the average for each age group is set at 100. The fractions close to the central distribution (usually 90-110) are in the normal range (normal range, see figures 6-6); (a) Scores below 70 at one end of the distribution fall within the category of intellectual disability; The scores, which are higher than 130 at the other end of the distribution, sometimes indicate that the test is a genius. Please take some time to study figures 6-6 in order to gain a better understanding of this concept.

p47.original: 因此，现在我们已不再通过心理年龄除以生理年龄来计算智商分数了。尽管现在的智商分数是“按曲线”计算的，但后来沿用了乘以100（能生成一个类似百分比的数字，易于理解）来表示比率的概念。这种计算方法只需在成年人之间进行比较，从而解决了成年人智商虚假下降的问题。
p47.en: Therefore, we no longer calculate IQ scores by dividing mental age by biological age. Although the current IQ score is “curve-based”, the concept of multiplier 100 (which can generate a similar percentage figure, which is easy to understand) was subsequently adopted. This method of calculation only needs to be compared between adults, thus addressing the problem of a fall in the intellectually false intelligence of adults.

p48.original: 另一个需要认识到的重要事情是，专家们不认为一个单一的智商分数，就像不同认知能力的综合测量那样，能准确地代表一个人的智力（Nisbett et al.，2012）。因此，大多数现代智力测验给出的分数至少反映了两个维度——通常是言语（词汇）和抽象推理方面的水平。
p48.en: Another important thing that needs to be recognized is that experts do not consider a single IQ score to be an accurate representation of a person's intelligence, as is the case with a combination of different cognitive abilities (Nisbett et al., 2012). Thus, the scores given in most modern intelligence tests reflect at least two dimensions — usually the level of words (the vocabulary) and abstract reasoning.

p51.original: 你已经知道了“正态曲线”指的是什么，你是否希望你的导师按这个曲线来给你评分？为什么？
p51.en: You already know what a normal curve means. Do you want your mentors to rate you against this curve? Why?

p52.original: 弗林效应 几十年前，研究人员詹姆斯·弗林（James Flynn）注意到，自从智力测验被发明以来，平均智商分数以大约每10年3分的速度递增；而每隔几年就对测验进行“重新标准化”以将平均智商维持在100的做法掩盖了这一事实（Flynn，1987）。这是否表明，随着时间的推移，我们会变得越来越聪明？表面上看，这种弗林效应（flynn effect）意味着，在你曾祖父母那个时代处于平均范围的人，放到今天可能会被认为有智力障碍！和大多数其他研究人员一样，弗林认为这样的结论很荒谬（Flynn，2003；Neisser et al.，1996）。那么，如何解释弗林效应呢？
p52.en: The Flynn effect. A few decades ago, the researcher James Flynn noted that since the brain test was invented, the average IQ score has increased at a rate of about three cents every 10 years; This fact is masked by the “re-standardization” of tests every few years to maintain the average IQ at 100 (Flynn, 1987). Does this mean that over time we will become smarter and smarter? On the face of it, the flynn effect means that people who were on average at the time of your great-grandparents may today be considered intellectually handicapped! Like most other researchers, Flynn finds this conclusion absurd (Flynn, 2003); (a) The right to freedom of expression; So, how do we explain the Flynn effect?

p53.original: 这种递增可能是多种因素共同作用的结果，包括更好的应试技巧、更复杂、有更多的心理刺激的社会环境（从电影到游戏，到计算机，再到手机等所有事物），更多的学校教育，以及更好的营养。弗林（Flynn，2007）本人指出，智力的不同成分的增长速率是不同的（如词汇量几乎没有任何变化），因此智商提高的部分原因是，社会开始重视和鼓励那些对智力有贡献的因素。例如，智力测验中有一个问题：“狗和兔子有什么相似之处？”[4]弗林说，一个世纪以前，这个问题的答案具有文化特异性：“你用狗来猎兔。”而现在，他说：“它们都是哺乳动物。”这两个不同的答案反映了不同的思考方式。弗林相信，智商测验分数的提高是20世纪教育体系的产物。这种教育体系教会儿童更有逻辑、更科学地思考——之后，再用智商分数作为对他们的奖励（Shea，2012）！
p53.en: This increase may be the result of a combination of factors, including better coping techniques, more complex, more psycho-stimulating social environments (from movies to games to computers to mobile phones, etc.), more schooling and better nutrition. Flynn, 2007 has pointed out that the growth rate of different components of intelligence is different (e.g., the volume of words has hardly changed), so the increase in IQ is partly due to the fact that society is beginning to focus on and encourage those factors that contribute to intelligence. For example, there's a question in the intelligence test: "What's the similarity between dogs and rabbits? The answer to this question was cultural, according to Flynn, a century ago: “You hunt rabbits with dogs. And now he says, "They're all mammals. These two different answers reflect different ways of thinking. Flynn believes that the increase in IQ scores is the product of the education system of the twentieth century. This educational system teaches children to think more logically and scientifically - then use IQ scores as a reward for them (Shea, 2012)!

p54.original: 然而，弗林效应可能正在放缓，至少在发达国家是这样的。自20世纪90年代中期以来，欧洲样本的测验分数就趋于稳定了，而且在某些情况下甚至有所下降（Teasdale & Owen，2008）。然而，在欠发达国家，人们的智商分数则会持续提高（Colom et al.，2007；Daley et al.，2003）。同时，自发现弗林效应以来对其的细致研究表明，智商分数的平均增长主要是低端分数显著增长的结果；在高端分数范围，则几乎没什么增长（Dutton & Lynn，2013；Teasdale & Owen，1987）。根据所有这些发现，一些理论学家认为，弗林效应可能确实标志着人们在获得教育、营养和认知刺激方面更加平等。如果这是真的，我们有望在未来几十年内看到，发达国家与发展中国家人们间的智商差距的缩小。
p54.en: However, the Flynn effect may be slowing down, at least in developed countries. Test scores in European samples have stabilized since the mid-1990s and have even declined in some cases (Teasdale & Owen, 2008). However, in less developed countries, people's IQ scores are expected to increase continuously (Colom et al., 2007); Daley et al., 2003. At the same time, detailed studies of the Flynn effect since its discovery show that the average growth in IQ scores is mainly the result of a significant increase in the low end scores; In the upper end range, there was little growth (Dutton & Lynn, 2013; Teasdale & Owen, 1987. On the basis of all these findings, some theorists believe that the Flynn effect may indeed mark greater equality in access to education, nutrition and cognitive stimulation. If that is true, we are expected to see in the coming decades a narrowing of the IQ gap between people in developed and developing countries.

p56.original: 斯坦福-比奈测验的成功激励了其他智商测验的发展。因此，心理学家现在有各种智力测量工具可选。其中最突出的是韦氏成人智力量表（Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale，WAIS）、韦氏儿童智力量表（Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children，WISC）和韦氏幼儿智力量表（Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence，WPPSI）。借助这些工具，心理学家大卫·韦克斯勒（David Wechsler）提供了一个测验工具箱，测量许多被认为是智力组成成分的技能，包括词汇、言语理解、算术能力、相似性（说出两个事物如何相似的能力）、数字广度（跟着测试者复述一系列数字）和积木设计（将带彩边的积木拼接起来以重现设计的能力）。正如本学习阶段的核心概念所指出的，这些测验通过评估各种任务表现来测量智力。
p56.en: The success of the Stanford-Bina test has stimulated the development of other IQ tests. As a result, psychologists now have a variety of intellectual measurement tools available. The most prominent of these are the Wechsler Adult Intelligence System, WAIS, Wechsler Intelligence System for Children, WISC and Wechsler Preschool and Child Scale of Intelligence, WPPSI. With these tools, a psychologist, David Wechsler, provides a test toolbox to measure many of the skills considered intellectual components, including vocabulary, speech understanding, numeracy, similarities (the ability to say how the two things are similar), numerical breadth (repeated with a series of numbers) and building blocks (the ability to combine the pieces of wood with coloured edges for re-engineering). As indicated in the core concept of this learning phase, these tests measure intelligence by assessing the performance of various tasks.

p57.original: 与斯坦福-比奈测验类似，韦氏测验也是个体测验。也就是说，它们每次只能测一个人。也有一些可用的团体智力测验，可以同时对大量学生施测。与斯坦福-比奈测验和韦氏测验不同的是，团体测验由纸笔测试组成，包括问题小册子和可用机器评分的答题卡。团体测验——尽管不如个体测验精准——的便利性使得智商测验及其他形式的学术评估广为普及。你很有可能在从1年级到12年级的学习过程中，已参加过多次这类测验，而没有意识到它们是什么。“试一试”版块中的这些题目，很像许多心理能力团体测验中的常用题目。
p57.en: Similar to the Stanford-Bina test, the Wedge test is also an individual test. In other words, they can only measure one person at a time. There are also available group intelligence tests that can be tested at the same time for a large number of students. Unlike the Stanford-Bina test and the Wedge test, group tests consist of paper and pen tests, including question booklets and machine-rated flashcards. The ease with which group tests, though less accurate than individual tests, have made IQ tests and other forms of academic evaluation widely available. It is very likely that you have taken such tests several times in the course of your studies, from the first to the twelfth grades, without being aware of what they are. These topics in the “test” section are very much like those commonly used in many mental competence group tests.

p99.original: 智商分数的确能够在一定程度上预测学业和某些其他方面的成功。除此之外，智商分数在确定儿童是否有“智力障碍”或“天赋”（我们将在下一个“心理学很有用”版块中更细致地考查这些概念）方面发挥着最重要的作用。除了以上这些用途之外，智商测验在诊断学习障碍方面的作用最为突出。杰克·纳格利里（Jack Naglieri）博士说，智力测验的问题是，智商分数并没有告诉我们对某特定儿童来说哪些干预策略可能有效果（Benson，2003）。为了解决这个问题，纳格利里和其他人正在开发一些测验，它们不那么强调单一分数（如智商），更强调对人们分类以提供不同的帮助建议（如识别阅读问题、知觉问题或注意障碍）。
p99.en: Indeed, IQ scores can provide some degree of predictability of academic success and some other aspects. In addition to this, IQ scores play the most important role in determining whether a child is “intellectually handicapped” or “natural” (which we will examine more closely in the next “Psychologically Useful” section). In addition to these uses, IQ tests play a prominent role in the diagnosis of learning disabilities. Dr. Jack Naglieri said that the problem with intelligence tests was that IQ scores did not tell us what intervention strategies could be effective for a particular child (Benson, 2003). In order to address this problem, Nagliri and others are developing tests that place less emphasis on a single score (e.g. IQ) and more emphasis on classifying people to provide different help advice (e.g. to identify reading problems, sensory problems or attention barriers).

p100.original: 心理学很有用 你能为特殊儿童做些什么
p100.en: Psychology works. What can you do for special children?

p101.original: 正如我们所指出的，智力障碍和天才位于智力谱系的两个极端。按照传统的设想，智力障碍的智商低于70分——约占人口的2%。天才的智商是人为划分为高于均值30分以上，即高于130分——约占人口的另外2%。在记住我们学到的智商测验的局限性的基础上，让我们简单看看这两个类别。
p101.en: As we have pointed out, intellectual disabilities and genius lie at two extremes of the intellectual spectrum. According to traditional assumptions, the intellectual disability has an IQ of less than 70 points - about 2 per cent of the population. Genius IQ is artificially classified at more than 30 minutes above the average, i.e. more than 130 points — about 2 per cent of the population. On the basis of the limitations of the IQ tests we have learned, let us briefly look at these two categories.

p103.original: 智力障碍的最新定义不再强调智商分数，而是关注人们与世界相处的实际能力（Robinson et al.，2000）。美国智力与发展障碍协会（American Association on Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities）将智力障碍定义为：在18岁之前就表现出来，在智力功能和适应行为方面有很大局限。智力功能上的局限可以通过70～75分的智商分数来测得；而适应行为包括社交技能、实践技能（如沟通、自理和职业技能）和概念技能（如理解金钱、语言和时间）。
p103.en: The latest definition of intellectual disability no longer emphasizes IQ scores, but focuses on the actual ability of people to live with the world (Robinson et al., 2000). The American Association of Intellectual and Developmental Impairments defines intellectual impairment as a significant limitation on intellectual function and adaptive behaviour, as manifested before the age of 18. Intellectual limitations can be measured by 70-75 points of IQ; Adaptive behaviour includes social skills, practical skills (e.g., communication, self-care and vocational skills) and conceptual skills (e.g., understanding money, language and time).

p105.original: 智力障碍有很多起因（Daily et al.，2000；Scott & Carran，1987）。有些智力障碍，如唐氏综合征（Down Syndrome），是因为遗传，因为我们已能确认是特定基因控制了这一缺陷。有些起因纯粹是环境，例如，胎儿酒精综合征的起因就包括母亲孕期酒精滥用导致的出生前脑部受损。其他的环境原因包括产后事故（造成大脑认知区域受损）、剥夺或忽视的环境条件（不能给发展中儿童提供智力增长所需的经验）。有些病例则原因不明。
p105.en: There are many causes of mental disorders (Daily et al., 2000); Scott & Carran, 1987. Some mental disorders, such as Down Syndrome, are genetic, because we can already identify specific genes that control this deficiency. Some of the causes are purely environmental, for example, foetal alcohol syndrome (FAIS) causes pre-birth brain damage due to alcohol abuse during pregnancy. Other environmental causes include post-natal accidents (which cause damage to brain cognitive areas), deprivation or neglect of environmental conditions (which do not provide developing children with the experience needed for intellectual growth). The reasons for some cases are unknown.

p107.original: 虽然研究已经找到了针对某些类型智力障碍的预防性措施，但是我们无法治愈它们。例如，对刚出生的婴儿进行一项常规简单检查就能识别出一种被称为苯丙酮尿症的隐性遗传疾病。在被及时发现的前提下，那些通常与苯丙酮尿症有关的疾病就可以通过一种特殊饮食来预防。一般来说，其他预防策略还有遗传咨询、孕期护理服务，以及新父母的教育（Scott & Carran，1987）。
p107.en: While research has identified preventive measures for certain types of intellectual disability, we cannot cure them. For example, a simple routine examination of a newborn can identify a hidden genetic disease known as phenylketone urine. Subject to timely detection, those diseases that are usually associated with phenylketonuria can be prevented through a special diet. In general, other preventive strategies include genetic counselling, pregnancy care services and the education of new parents (Scott & Carran, 1987).

p108.original: 除了预防外，特殊教育课程还能帮助那些智力障碍患者学习职业技能和独立生活技能。与此同时，生物学家希望有朝一日能够用目前正在构思的疗法来治疗基于遗传的智力障碍。例如，基因治疗可能涉及将健康基因拼接到一种良性病毒中，以“感染”某些类型的智力障碍患者的所有细胞，并置换缺陷基因。目前，智力障碍的基因治疗至少还需要几年时间。
p108.en: In addition to prevention, special education curricula help people with intellectual disabilities to learn vocational skills and independent life skills. At the same time, biologists hope that one day they will be able to treat genetic-based mental disorders with the therapy that is currently being conceived. For example, gene therapy may involve the enslaving of healthy genes into a benign virus, “infecting” all cells of certain types of persons with intellectual impairment and replacing defective genes. At present, genetic treatment for intellectual disabilities takes at least a few years.

p109.original: 现在，如果你有一个身患智力障碍的孩子，你可以做些什么？由于出生时婴儿的神经系统还没有发育成熟，而且许多身心发展都发生在生命的前几年，因此，早期干预的效果可能最好。感觉刺激和社会互动这样的心理学干预方法十分重要。加上适宜的教育课程带来的效果，有智力障碍的孩子的智商有望提高15分（Robinson et al.，2000）。
p109.en: Now, what can you do if you have a child with a mental disability? Since the nervous system of the baby at birth is not yet mature and many physical and mental developments take place in the first years of life, early intervention may be the most effective. Psychological interventions such as sensory stimulation and social interaction are important. Together with the effects of appropriate educational curricula, the IQ of children with intellectual disabilities is expected to increase by 15 points (Robinson et al., 2000).

p110.original: 特殊奥林匹克运动会（the Special Olympics）为智力障碍儿童（和其他残障儿童）提供了一个充分利用自身能力和建立自尊的机会。
p110.en: The Special Olympics provide an opportunity for children with intellectual disabilities (and other disabled children) to make full use of their abilities and build self-esteem.

p111.original: 事实上，丰富的环境对智力障碍儿童的帮助可能和对天才儿童的帮助一样。由特殊教育教师、言语治疗师、教育心理学家、医生和其他专家组成的团队可以设计课程来教会学生充分利用他们拥有的能力，而不是被他们的障碍所束缚（Schroeder et al.，1987）。行为矫正课程成效显著，使得许多智力障碍公民学会了照顾自己，并获得了能使他们独立生活的职业技能（Landesman & Butterfield，1987）。
p111.en: In fact, a rich environment can be as helpful to children with intellectual disabilities as it is to gifted children. Teams of special education teachers, speech therapists, educational psychologists, doctors and other specialists can design curricula to teach students to take full advantage of their abilities, rather than being held hostage by their barriers (Schroeder et al., 1987). The behavioural correction course was very effective, enabling many citizens with intellectual disabilities to learn to take care of themselves and acquire vocational skills that would enable them to live independently (Landesman & Butterfield, 1987).

p113.original: 智力谱系的另一端是“天才”，他们智商极高，通常被定义为位于人口前1%或2%的人（Robinson et al.，2000）。但是，高智商会给其拥有者的生活带来优势吗？对天才个体的长期观察表明，这个问题的答案是肯定的。
p113.en: The other end of the intellectual spectrum is “genius”, who have a very high IQ, usually defined as a person who is 1% or 2% of the population (Robinson et al., 2000). But does the Chamber bring advantages to the lives of its owners? Long-term observations of talented individuals suggest that the answer to this question is yes.

p115.original: 对天才个体进行的最广泛的研究始于1921年，它是在路易斯·推孟——就是将比奈和西蒙智商测验引入美国的那个人——的指导下展开的（Leslie，2000）。推孟从在加利福尼亚的学校接受测验的大量儿童中选出了1528名得分接近智商范围顶端的儿童。他的纵向研究项目对这些儿童进行了从入学到成年的追踪。在他们的一生中，推孟定期对他们进行重测，收集有关他们成就和适应模式的信息。由此产生的数十年的数据揭示了有关天才本质的许多信息。推孟的天才儿童几乎在学校中都表现出色，正如人们从智商和学业成就间的强相关中所预期的那样。推孟还提到样本中的儿童拥有健康和幸福，虽然更新的证据表明，极端天才儿童对某些身体和心理障碍具有易感性（Winner，2000）。
p115.en: The most extensive study of talented individuals began in 1921, under the guidance of Louis Thémon — the person who introduced the Bene and Simon IQ tests to the United States (Leslie, 2000). From the large number of children tested in schools in California, Thémon selected 1528 children close to the top of the IQ range. His longitudinal research project tracked these children from school to adulthood. Throughout their lives, they are regularly re-measured to gather information on their achievements and adaptation patterns. The resulting decades of data reveal much of the information about the nature of genius. Talented children of Thimphu are performing well in almost all schools, as expected from the strong correlation between IQ and academic achievement. Tamong also mentioned the health and well-being of children in the sample, although updated evidence suggests that children with extreme talents are susceptible to certain physical and psychological disorders (Winner, 2000).

p116.original: 随着他们成年，这个天才群体继续沿着成功的道路发展。他们中出现了异常多的科学家、作家和专业人士。他们总共发表了2000余篇科研论文，申请了235项发明专利，并撰写了92本书。到中年时，他们之中超过86%的男性从事着高社会地位的职业（Terman & Oden，1959）。
p116.en: As they mature, this gifted group continues to follow the path of success. An extraordinary number of scientists, writers and professionals have emerged. In total, they published more than 2,000 scientific papers, applied for 235 invention patents and wrote 92 books. By mid-year, more than 86 per cent of them were in socially advanced occupations (Terman & Oden, 1959).

p117.original: 然而，尽管这些高智商样本取得了上述这些成就，却没有人达到阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦、玛丽·居里（Marie Curie）、列昂纳多·达·芬奇（Leonardo da Vinci）或传奇的英国首相玛格丽特·撒切尔（Margaret Thatcher）的水平（他们的智商分数是180）。高智商也不能确保健康或地位。事实上，推孟样本中的许多人过着普通的、与常人无异的生活。最明显的成功者除了拥有高智商外，似乎还有着超强的动机，以及在家里或学校有特别激励他们的人（Goleman，1980；Oden，1968）——这些特征与“天才”的标志性特征相同。
p117.en: However, despite these achievements, none of these highly intelligent samples have reached the level of Albert Einstein, Marie Curie, Leonardo da Vinci or the legendary British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher, whose IQ score is 180. Nor does high IQ ensure health or status. In fact, many of the people in the Pyramid sample live ordinary and normal lives. The most obvious success has seemed to have a super-intelligent motive in addition to high IQ, as well as a particular incentive for them at home or in school (Goleman, 1980); Oden, 1968) - These characteristics are the same as the emblematic characteristics of “genius”.

p119.original: 想象你是一个智商分数很高（如145分）的天才儿童的父母。以下哪个是最好的行动方案？
p119.en: Imagine you're the parent of a gifted child with a high IQ score, like 145. Which of the following is the best course of action?

p120.original: 给孩子报名参加特殊的课外课程；
p120.en: (b) To enrol children in special extra-curricular courses;

p121.original: 聘请家教辅导孩子完成家庭作业；
p121.en: (b) The recruitment of tutors to help the child complete his or her homework;

p122.en: (b) To send children to private schools;

p124.original: 专家怎么说？不要因为孩子的智商分数而急于给孩子报特殊课程或提供其他“帮助”（Csikszentmihalyi et al.，1993；Wong & Csikszentmihalyi，1991）。将孩子推向一个不符合他们兴趣的目标，可能会消灭他们的好奇心。很有可能，你已经在给孩子提供一个供其先天能力蓬勃发展的环境了。所以，不要做任何轻率和激进的改变。
p124.en: What did the expert say? Do not rush to give children special courses or other “helps” because of their IQ scores (Csikszentmihalyi et al., 1993); Wong & Csikszentmihalyi, 1991. To push children towards a goal that does not suit their interests may eliminate their curiosity. It's possible you're already providing a child with an environment in which he/she can flourish. So do not make any reckless and radical changes.

p125.original: 最重要的是，避免让孩子因其不同寻常的能力和高智商而感到与众不同。部分原因是因为，天才儿童身上的某些人格特质——特别是花时间独处、研究自己兴趣的倾向——已经比其他孩子更可能遭受社交和情绪障碍的困扰了（Winner，2000）。你也不应该为你对孩子智力做出的遗传贡献而感到沾沾自喜。
p125.en: Above all, it is important to avoid making children feel different because of their extraordinary abilities and high IQ. This is partly due to the fact that some of the personality characteristics of gifted children — especially the tendency to spend time alone and to study their own interests — are more likely to suffer from social and emotional disorders than other children (Winner, 2000). And you shouldn't be complacent about your genetic contribution to the child's intelligence.

p126.original: 请记住，智力涉及先天与后天的交互作用；此外，智商测验测试的仅是人类能力的一小部分。其他的孩子可能在未被测试的智力区域具有同样惊人的能力。事实上，许多天才个体都没有被学校发现，是因为他们的卓越才能主要表现在美术或音乐领域——正式的能力测验几乎不会测试这些领域。
p126.en: Remember that intelligence involves the interaction between the birth and the day after; Moreover, IQ tests are only a small part of human capacity. Other children may have equally amazing capabilities in untested intellectual areas. Indeed, many talented individuals are not found in school because their excellence is manifested mainly in the field of fine arts or music — areas that official competency tests hardly test.

p127.original: 还要记住，高智商并不能保证高动机、高创造力或人生成功。它所保证的只是一个智力上的机遇。
p127.en: It is also important to remember that high IQ does not guarantee high motivation, high creativity or life success. It guarantees only an intellectual opportunity.

p128.original: 那么，该如何对待一个聪明的孩子？你不需要做什么特别的事情，就与你知道孩子的智商分数之前一样，一切如常即可。
p128.en: So, what about a smart kid? You don't have to do anything special, just like you did before you knew the kids' IQ scores.
